title: Preview of a forthcoming supernova

geometryEvidence.reference: A picture of the sky: the plane is the picture's own tangent plane, perpendicular to the sight line through the picture's centre, so it faces the Sun. That centre is 2.1 arcsec from the star, which is the whole of the recipe's inclination. Not the orientation of the nebula, which is the surface's.

registration.method: The file's embedded sky tags for scale and direction, 0.0248 arcsec per pixel and north 34.98° left of vertical, and the star for place: the middle of the picture's saturated pixels, pixel 627, 525, is set at Eta Carinae's catalogued place, so the frame's centre is 161.2656327°, -59.684052°.

displayModel: Inside the outline of the surface Steffen et al. (2014) made, the picture's light lies on that surface, a closed mesh placed with its pole 41 degrees from the sight line toward position angle 310 degrees (Smith 2006). A sight line enters and leaves each lobe: the side nearest the Sun holds the picture, and each side behind it, which the picture does not show, repeats the picture sight line by sight line. The central star's glare is part of the picture and lies on the surface with it. Outside the outline the picture lies on one plane through the star, facing the Sun. The surface is drawn as meshes of flat patches.
coverage: The published frame inside a circle about the star: the picture fades out between 10.3 and 11.4 arcsec, the largest circle the frame holds, so no straight edge shows.

acquisition.operation: Download the publisher's JPEG; no crop or resample.
